## Assessment: Vimentin (VIM) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt).** Vimentin, gene *VIM*, UniProt accession P08670, is a 466-aa protein whose catalogued function involves stabilizing type I collagen mRNAs with LARP6. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P08670/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold).** The predicted structure has a mean pLDDT of 77.1/100 ("Confident" band). Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P08670 — Note: this reflects structure-prediction reliability for the unmodified protein, not autoantigen status.

**Autoantigen evidence (literature).** The literature search returned direct, on-topic evidence that the **citrullinated/mutated form of vimentin is an established ACPA target in RA**:
- A scoping review specifically on **anti-mutated citrullinated vimentin (anti-MCV) antibodies in RA**, examining their diagnostic and clinical significance — the existence of a named, clinically studied antibody system directly against (mutated) citrullinated vimentin establishes it as a recognized RA autoantigen. Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42496286
- A review documenting that autoantibodies and T cells in RA target **citrullinated and homocitrullinated antigens**. Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443

**Caveats for your review.** The UniProt entry holds the *unmodified* protein, which is expected — ACPA recognize the citrullinated form, and this does not weaken the case. The clearest, most direct evidence here is the anti-MCV (anti-mutated citrullinated vimentin) antibody literature, which names vimentin as the specific target. The evidence is consistent (no conflict), though I note it rests primarily on literature titles rather than full-text mechanistic detail.

**Summary.** Tool evidence establishes that citrullinated/mutated vimentin is a recognized ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) target in RA, including a dedicated clinical antibody test (anti-MCV).

VERDICT: YES

I now have enough tool evidence for an assessment.

## Assessment: Alpha-enolase (ENO1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Alpha-enolase, gene **ENO1**, UniProt accession **P06733**, 434 aa. Normally a glycolytic/metabolic and transcriptional-regulatory protein; mammalian enolase is built from α, β, γ isozyme subunits forming homo-/heterodimers. [https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P06733/entry]
- Note: UniProt holds the *unmodified* protein, so it does not by itself describe citrullination — this is expected and not a reason to reject autoantigen status.

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT **97.6/100 ("Very high")** — the predicted 3D structure is highly reliable. [https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P06733]

**Literature evidence linking ENO1 to RA autoimmunity**
- A 2019 study explicitly evaluates **anti-citrullinated α-enolase peptide 1 (anti-CEP-1) antibody in the diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis** — i.e., the citrullinated form of alpha-enolase is used/tested as an RA diagnostic autoantibody target. [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/31471340]
- A 2022 cohort study reports **"anti-citrullinated protein antibody specificities ... in early rheumatoid arthritis"** examining anti-CEP-1 among ACPA fine specificities. [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/35532073]
- A 2017 paper, **"Antibodies against citrullinated alpha enolase peptides,"** treats citrullinated alpha-enolase as a recognized ACPA target (studied here in Sjögren's by extension from RA). [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/28919520]

**Interpretation**
The tool evidence consistently identifies **citrullinated alpha-enolase (particularly the CEP-1 epitope)** as a recognized ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) target in RA, including its use as a diagnostic marker. This meets the criterion for an established RA autoantigen (its citrullinated form is an established ACPA target). Evidence is consistent across multiple papers, not conflicting.

*For expert review: the citation trail above comes directly from the tools; I have not added outside knowledge. If you want firmer sensitivity/specificity figures for anti-CEP-1, the 2019 diagnostic-value paper would be the one to pull in full.*

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt).** FGA encodes the Fibrinogen alpha chain (UniProt P02671, 866 aa). It is cleaved by thrombin and polymerizes together with fibrinogen beta (FGB) and gamma (FGG) to form the insoluble fibrin matrix central to hemostasis. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02671/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold).** The AlphaFold predicted model has a mean pLDDT of 60.3/100 ("Low" confidence) — expected for a largely elongated/fibrous and partly disordered protein. This is a note on model reliability only and does not bear on antigen status. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02671

**Literature evidence for RA autoantigen status.** In RA, the dominant autoantibody system is ACPA, which recognizes citrullinated proteins. The literature returned by my searches establishes that:
- Autoantibodies and T cells in RA target citrullinated antigens, and citrullinated fibrinogen is discussed among the classic citrullinated autoantigens. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- Reviews of protective and pathogenic antibodies to citrullinated antigens in RA cover citrullinated fibrinogen as a target. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
- Work on post-translational neoantigen generation and anti-modified protein antibodies in RA frames citrullinated fibrinogen among the recognized modified self-proteins. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363 ; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42522109

Taken together, the tools confirm FGA is a chain of the fibrinogen complex, and the literature establishes citrullinated fibrinogen as a recognized ACPA target in RA. Per the stated rule, a chain/subunit of a protein established as an RA autoantibody target is itself an established autoantigen.

**Caveats for your review.** The literature hits are broad reviews rather than a single primary paper naming "FGA/alpha chain" in isolation, and ACPA generally target the citrullinated form (not the native UniProt sequence). The evidence is consistent and points one direction, but you may wish to confirm chain-specific citrullination epitope data in a primary source.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen beta chain (FGB) as an RA autoantigen

**What the tools returned**

**Protein identity (UniProt, https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02675/entry):**
- Fibrinogen beta chain, gene FGB, accession P02675, 491 aa.
- It is one of three non-identical chains (alpha/FGA, beta/FGB, gamma/FGG) that assemble into the fibrinogen heterohexamer, which polymerizes into fibrin.

**Structure (AlphaFold, https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02675):**
- Mean pLDDT 84.1/100 — "Confident." This is background structural information on the unmodified protein; it does not by itself speak to autoantigen status.

**Literature evidence linking it to RA autoimmunity:**
- Multiple reviews establish that **citrullinated antigens** are the central targets of ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies) in RA — e.g., "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443) and "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571).
- Importantly, the citrullinome paper explicitly names **fibrinogen** among the citrullinated antigenic targets in RA: "The rheumatoid arthritis citrullinome is enriched in antigenic complement proteins" (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41593658).

**Interpretation**
- UniProt confirms FGB is a bona fide chain of the fibrinogen heterohexamer (P02675). The literature establishes that citrullinated fibrinogen is an ACPA target in RA. Under the rule that an individual chain of a multi-chain target protein is itself an established autoantigen when the tools establish the parent protein as the RA target, FGB qualifies.
- **Caveat for expert review:** My tool searches confirmed fibrinogen (the parent molecule) as a citrullinated ACPA target, but did not return a paper isolating the *beta chain* epitope specifically. The verdict rests on the chain-of-a-target rule plus the generic citrullinated-fibrinogen evidence. If you need chain-level specificity, I'd suggest a focused full-text search for defined citrullinated FGB peptide epitopes.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibrinogen gamma chain (FGG) as an RA autoantigen

**What the protein is**
- UniProt confirms **FGG** encodes the **Fibrinogen gamma chain** (accession P02679, 453 aa). Critically, it is one of three non-identical chains (alpha/FGA, beta/FGB, gamma/FGG) that assemble into the fibrinogen heterohexamer. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02679/entry
- AlphaFold predicts its structure with a "Confident" mean pLDDT of 85.5/100. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02679

**Link to RA autoimmunity (ACPA)**
- Multiple literature results establish that **citrullinated antigens are targets of ACPA in RA** — e.g., "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" (James et al., 2026) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443 and "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" (Sareila et al., 2026) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571
- Most specifically, a paper explicitly names **citrullinated fibrinogen as an immunodominant target in RA patients**: "Immune reactivity directed against the carbamylated fibrinogen α chain does not cross-react with **citrullinated fibrinogen immunodominant peptides in patients with rheumatoid arthritis**" (Brevet et al., 2024) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/39389619

**How this applies to FGG specifically**
- The tools establish that (citrullinated) **fibrinogen** is an immunodominant ACPA target in RA (MED/39389619), and UniProt establishes that FGG (the gamma chain) is a constituent chain of that fibrinogen molecule (P02679). Per the chain/subunit rule, an individual chain of a parent protein shown to be an RA autoantibody target is itself an established RA autoantigen.

**Caveats for your review**
- My searches did not surface a title quantifying anti-citrullinated-fibrinogen-gamma antibody prevalence in isolation; the direct fibrinogen-RA evidence (MED/39389619) refers to "citrullinated fibrinogen" collectively and highlights the α chain in its carbamylation comparison. The gamma-chain inference rests on the chain-membership rule plus the established fibrinogen-ACPA link, rather than a gamma-chain-specific antibody study. An expert may wish to confirm gamma-chain-specific epitope data.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Fibronectin (FN1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** Fibronectin, gene FN1, accession P02751, 2,477 aa. UniProt describes its function in muscle secretion, liver autophagy, and insulin signaling via integrin receptors — it does **not** mention any role as an RA autoantigen or autoantibody target. (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02751/entry)

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold):** Mean pLDDT 69.7/100 — "Low" confidence band. This reflects prediction quality for this large multidomain protein and is not relevant to autoantigen status. (https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02751)

**Literature (Europe PMC):** I ran five targeted searches combining fibronectin/FN1 with terms for citrullination, ACPA, autoantibodies, and RA. None of the returned papers specifically established fibronectin as an ACPA target, an RF target, or any other autoantibody target in RA. The results were general RA/citrullination reviews and papers on *other* autoantigens:
- A citrullination neoantigen review (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42694363)
- PAD4/citrullination mechanism reviews (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42222154, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42162237)
- Papers naming *other* autoantigens — collagen type II (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42939478), aggrecan (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42502362), fibrinogen (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/40943137)

**Conclusion:** My tools returned no evidence linking fibronectin (citrullinated or otherwise) to RA autoantibody responses. UniProt gives no RA autoimmune annotation, and refined literature searches surfaced other autoantigens but never established fibronectin as one. This is an absence of established evidence in the tool results — not proof it can never be an autoantigen. An expert may wish to consult specialized ACPA-proteomics literature, as my search tool may not index every relevant primary study.

VERDICT: NO

The refined search returned directly relevant evidence. Here is my assessment.

## Assessment: Type II collagen (COL2A1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** The query resolves to Collagen alpha-1(II) chain, gene COL2A1, accession P02458, a 1487-aa protein specific to cartilaginous tissue, forming homotrimers of alpha-1(II) chains. [https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P02458/entry]

**Structural note (AlphaFold):** The predicted structure has a mean pLDDT of 52.1/100 ("Low" confidence) [https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P02458]. This is expected for a fibrillar collagen (long repetitive triple-helical sequence) and does not bear on its autoantigen status — it's just a caveat about the 3D model.

**Evidence linking it to RA autoimmunity (literature):**
- A 2026 study explicitly examined "Citrullination of Collagen Type II and Epitope-Specific Antibody Responses in Rheumatoid Arthritis," comparing antibody responses in RA — directly establishing citrullinated type II collagen as a target of epitope-specific autoantibodies in RA patients. [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42939478]
- A review of "Protective and Pathogenic Antibodies to Citrullinated Antigens" from the Holmdahl group (long associated with collagen-induced arthritis and anti-collagen antibodies) is in the same RA/citrullinated-antigen space. [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571]
- The collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mouse model — in which immunization with type II collagen drives arthritis — appears repeatedly in RA model literature. [https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13665015]

**Interpretation:** The tool evidence shows that type II collagen, including its citrullinated form, is a recognized target of autoantibody responses in RA patients, consistent with the ACPA system. The COL2A1 product (collagen alpha-1(II) chain) is the chain that makes up the type II collagen homotrimer per UniProt, so evidence establishing type II collagen as the target applies to this protein.

**Caveats for expert review:** My most specific supporting paper is a single comparative study plus related reviews/models; I did not retrieve large clinical cohort prevalence data in these results. Anti-type II collagen antibodies are generally regarded as less sensitive/specific for RA than anti-CCP/ACPA against other antigens, so weigh this in context. Still, the tools returned direct evidence establishing it as a recognized autoantibody target in RA.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Filaggrin (FLG) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** Filaggrin, gene *FLG*, UniProt accession P20930, 4061 aa. Its annotated function is aggregating keratin intermediate filaments during terminal differentiation of mammalian epidermis. UniProt provides no RA/autoimmune annotation in the entry itself (unmodified protein). Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P20930/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold):** Could not be assessed — the AlphaFold API returned a 404 (no structure available for P20930), likely because of the protein's very large size / repetitive nature. I therefore cannot report a pLDDT confidence. *(Fail honestly: no structure data available.)*

**Literature evidence linking filaggrin to RA autoimmunity:**
- A paper explicitly titled **"Significance of antibodies to filaggrin in diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis"** (Ai Maixing, Leng Xiaomei, Zeng Xiaofeng) directly documents anti-filaggrin antibodies in RA diagnosis. https://europepmc.org/article/CBA/642605
- **"An Overview of the Intrinsic Role of Citrullination in Autoimmune Disorders"** (Alghamdi et al., 2019) covers the role of citrullination (the modification that converts filaggrin into an ACPA target) in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/31886309
- Multiple retrieved reviews confirm that **citrullinated proteins are the targets of ACPA, the hallmark autoantibodies of RA** (e.g., James et al. 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443; Stalman & van der Woude 2026, https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42522109).

**Interpretation:** The tools returned a publication specifically demonstrating anti-filaggrin antibodies in RA diagnosis, plus supporting literature establishing citrullinated proteins as the ACPA target system in RA. This is consistent with filaggrin (in its citrullinated form) being a recognized ACPA target. The evidence is from literature titles/abstracts rather than a curated UniProt disease annotation, so an expert should confirm the primary sources before clinical use.

**Caveats for human review:** UniProt holds only the unmodified protein (no RA annotation), and the AlphaFold structure was unavailable. The autoantigen case rests on the literature hits above, not on database disease fields.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H4 (gene H4C1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt).** The query resolves to Histone H4, UniProt accession P62805, a 103–amino-acid core nucleosome component (two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3, H4 form the histone octamer). The UniProt entry describes its chromatin/transcription role but makes **no mention of any autoantigen or RA association**. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P62805/entry

**Structure (AlphaFold).** The predicted structure for P62805 has a mean pLDDT of 89.8/100 ("Confident"). This is a structural-quality metric only and says nothing about autoantigen status. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P62805

**Literature (Europe PMC).** Across several targeted searches (citrullinated histone H4, anti-histone antibodies in RA, citrullinated histones/NETs as ACPA targets), the tool returned many RA/citrullination/NETosis papers, but **none that explicitly establishes histone H4 — or the histone family — as a recognized ACPA or other autoantibody target in RA.** The nearest hits are contextual rather than establishing:
- "Autoantibodies and T Cells Target Citrullinated and Homocitrullinated Antigens in Rheumatoid Arthritis" — general to citrullinated antigens, histone H4 not specified. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443
- "Anti-Carbamylated Protein Antibodies Stabilize Carbamylated Histone **H3**..." — concerns histone H3, not H4. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41930627
- NET-focused reviews mentioning citrullinated histones broadly in RA pathogenesis, e.g. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41376642

**Interpretation (for your review).** My tools confirm the protein's identity and structure but did **not** return evidence that specifically establishes citrullinated histone H4 as an ACPA target, nor that the histone family is an established RA autoantibody target. Histones are frequently discussed in the RA/NETosis/citrullination literature, and histone H3 (a different protein) appears as a modified target in one returned paper — but I cannot, on the current tool evidence, substitute H3 or "histones in general" for an established H4-specific or family-level autoantigen claim. This is an absence of establishing evidence, not conflicting evidence. A reasonable next step would be a focused full-text search for primary studies profiling serum ACPA reactivity against citrullinated histone H4 peptides.

VERDICT: NO

## Assessment: Histone H2B (gene H2BC4) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (confirmed by tools):**
- UniProt confirms H2BC4 encodes **Histone H2B type 1-C/E/F/G/I** (accession P62807, 126 aa), a core nucleosome component — the nucleosome octamer contains two each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4 [https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P62807/entry].
- AlphaFold predicted structure confidence is **"Confident" (mean pLDDT 88.1/100)** [https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P62807]. (Structure quality is unrelated to autoantigen status; included for completeness.)

**Literature evidence:**
My searches did **not** return a clear, specific result establishing citrullinated histone H2B as a recognized ACPA (or other autoantibody) target in RA. What I did find was adjacent/indirect:
- Multiple reviews link citrullinated histones and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) to RA pathology, but as mechanistic/pathogenic contributors rather than establishing H2B specifically as a defined antibody target — e.g. NET reviews [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41335221; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41703739] and "Extracellular histones aggravate autoimmune arthritis" (a pathogenic-role study, not an autoantibody-target study) [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36032105].
- The specific anti-histone autoantibody data returned concerned **histone H3** (anti-H3K9 and anti-lactylated H3), not H2B [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42938145; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41073397].
- General reviews on citrullination/homocitrullination as ACPA targets in RA exist [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36555449; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443], but none in my results names histone H2B as an established target, nor did any tool result clearly establish "citrullinated histones" as a family that is a confirmed ACPA target (which would let me classify H2B by membership).

**Bottom line (for your review):** My tools confirm what H2B *is* (a core nucleosome histone) and show citrullinated histones/NETs are broadly implicated in RA biology — but they did **not** return evidence specifically establishing histone H2B (or the histone family) as a recognized RA autoantibody target. The evidence is suggestive of involvement in RA-related NET/citrullination biology but falls short of establishing H2B as a defined autoantigen. Given the rule to treat absence of established evidence as NO, I classify accordingly. A useful next step would be to retrieve full abstracts of the Haro 2022 review [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/36555449] and James 2026 [https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443] to check whether they name specific histone subtypes.

VERDICT: NO

## Assessment: Histone H3.1 (gene H3C1) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt):** Histone H3.1 is a core nucleosome component, UniProt accession P68431, 136 aa. The nucleosome is a histone octamer containing two molecules each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P68431/entry

**Structure (AlphaFold):** Predicted structure confidence is "Confident" (mean pLDDT 86.0/100). This is background structural information, not evidence of autoantigen status. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P68431

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC):** The key point in RA is that ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibodies) recognize the *citrullinated* form of proteins. My searches returned direct evidence linking citrullinated histone H3 to RA autoimmunity:

- A 2026 study measured **positivity rates and serum levels of antibodies against histone H3 (Lys9 and its lactylated form) in rheumatoid arthritis**, directly treating histone H3 as an antibody target in RA. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42938145
- Histone H3 is a principal protein in **neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)**, which are citrullinated by PAD enzymes; multiple RA papers describe NETs and citrullination (including PAD2/PAD4-mediated protein citrullination) as central to RA autoimmunity. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42162237 ; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41376642
- Reviews on **autoantibodies/T cells targeting citrullinated antigens in RA** and **antibodies to citrullinated antigens** frame citrullinated nuclear/NET proteins as RA targets. https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443 ; https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42649571

**Caveat / human-in-the-loop note:** My searches did not return a single paper whose title isolates "anti-citrullinated histone H3.1 (H3C1 isoform)" as a defined, quantified ACPA specificity. The strongest direct hit (MED/42938145) measures anti-histone H3 antibodies in RA, and the surrounding NET/citrullination literature establishes citrullinated histone H3 as an autoimmune target in RA. Because UniProt confirms H3.1 is one of the H3 molecules forming the nucleosome/NET substrate, and the literature establishes histone H3 (citrullinated, within NETs) as an RA autoantibody target, the evidence supports autoantigen status. An expert should review the primary papers to confirm the specific isoform relevance, as the tools point to "histone H3" generally rather than the H3.1/H3C1 variant exclusively.

On balance, the tools returned published evidence that histone H3 — citrullinated and NET-derived — is targeted by autoantibodies in RA, and H3.1 is an H3 molecule.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: Histone H2A type 1 (gene *H2AC11*) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Histone H2A type 1, gene **H2AC11**, accession **P0C0S8**, 130 aa. It is a **core component of the nucleosome**, part of the histone octamer containing two molecules each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P0C0S8/entry
- (Note: my first lookup of "H2AC11" and "Histone H2A" misfired — "H2AC11" was read as an accession, and "Histone H2A" returned USP22, a deubiquitinase that acts *on* histones, not the histone itself. The correct entry was confirmed via "HIST1H2AG" and the accession P0C0S8.)

**Structure confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT **91.1 / 100 — "Very high"** confidence for the predicted (unmodified) structure. Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P0C0S8
- (This reflects the native protein; AlphaFold does not model citrullination.)

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC)**
- Histones are established ACPA targets in RA: *"Characterization of Autoantigens Targeted by Anti-Citrullinated Protein Antibodies In Vivo: Prominent Role for Epitopes Derived from Histone 4 Proteins"* (Meng et al., 2016) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/27788229
- **Citrullinated histones as a class** are recognized autoantibody targets in NET-associated autoimmunity including RA: anti-citrullinated histone monoclonal **CIT-013** (van der Linden et al., 2023) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/38031350
- RA synovial B-cell clones react with **neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) antigens** (histones are major NET constituents): Corsiero et al., 2020 https://europepmc.org/article/MED/32221039 ; and NET/citrullinated antigens as RA autoantibody targets: James et al., 2026 https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42740443

**Interpretation**
My tools establish that (1) H2A type 1 is a member of the core histone family / nucleosome octamer (UniProt P0C0S8), and (2) citrullinated histones are an established class of ACPA/autoantibody targets in RA (Meng 2016; CIT-013, 2023; NET-antigen reactivity, 2020). Under the family-membership criterion, this supports classifying H2A as an RA autoantigen.

**Caveat for your review:** The strongest *subtype-specific* published evidence my searches returned names histone **H4** (and carbamylated H3) explicitly; I did not retrieve a paper naming "histone H2A" individually as the autoantibody target. The YES rests on H2A being an established member of the histone family that is collectively an ACPA/NET-antigen target, not on an H2A-specific serology study. If you need H2A-specific confirmation, a focused query for citrullinated-H2A epitope-mapping or peptide-array ACPA studies would be the next step.

VERDICT: YES

## Assessment: BiP/GRP78 (gene HSPA5) as an RA autoantigen

**Protein identity (UniProt)**
- Confirmed as "Endoplasmic reticulum chaperone BiP", gene HSPA5, accession **P11021**, 654 aa. The UniProt functional annotation covers its chaperone/receptor roles but does not itself mention RA or autoimmunity. Source: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11021/entry

**Structural confidence (AlphaFold)**
- Mean pLDDT 90.0/100 — "Confident" band, so the predicted 3D structure is reliable. (Structural quality only; not evidence of autoantigen status.) Source: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P11021

**Literature evidence (Europe PMC)**
- A paper explicitly titles BiP **"a putative autoantigen in rheumatoid arthritis,"** describing an immune (CD8 T-cell/IL-10) response to it (Bodman-Smith et al., 2003). Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/12709539
- Follow-up work from the same group characterizes BiP as a stress protein immunomodulator relevant to inflammatory arthritis (Corrigall et al., 2004). Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/15077298
- A review frames BiP/ER-stress proteins within RA pathogenesis (Park et al., 2014). Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/24431899
- A 2025 study examines intracellular/extracellular GRP78/BiP and their association with RA disease activity and progression (Liu et al., 2025). Source: https://europepmc.org/article/MED/39851332

**Interpretation and caveats (for your review)**
- The tools returned multiple published papers that explicitly treat BiP/GRP78 as an autoantigen in RA — one titles it a "putative autoantigen in rheumatoid arthritis" and others build a sustained body of immunological work around it. This supports recognition of BiP as an RA autoantigen.

## Assessment: IgG1 Fc (gene IGHG1, UniProt P01857)

**What the tools establish:**

**1. Protein identity (UniProt).** IGHG1 encodes "Immunoglobulin heavy constant gamma 1" (P01857), the **constant region of the IgG1 heavy chain**. UniProt explicitly states this constant region "interacts (via the fragment crystallizable, **Fc**) with receptors on innate immune cells and the complement system." So IGHG1 *is* the IgG1 Fc/constant region. (https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P01857/entry)

**2. Link to RA autoimmunity (literature).** In RA, one of the two main antibody systems is **rheumatoid factor (RF)**, which by definition targets the Fc (constant) region of IgG. The literature search returned RA-specific evidence that RF binding is a defining feature of RA:
- "Different rheumatoid factor binding patterns distinguish between Sjögren's disease with or without associated RA" (2025) — RF binding studied in the RA context (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/40545271)
- A 2026 study on RF-mediated modulation of IgG Fc–FcRn recycling and immune-complex uptake, directly tying RF to the IgG Fc region (https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42827951)

Because the tools establish that (a) RF is a core RA autoantibody whose target is the IgG Fc/constant region, and (b) IGHG1/P01857 is precisely that IgG1 heavy-chain constant (Fc) region, IGHG1 qualifies as an established RA autoantigen under the RF-target criterion.

**3. Structure (AlphaFold).** The predicted structure of P01857 has a mean pLDDT of 86.7 ("Confident" band) — a reliable model of the unmodified constant region (https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/entry/P01857).

**Caveats for your review:** The literature tool did not return a single paper stating in one sentence "IGHG1 Fc is the RF autoantigen"; the conclusion rests on combining the UniProt identity (IGHG1 = IgG1 Fc/constant region) with RA literature showing RF targets IgG Fc. The evidence is consistent and not conflicting, but the RF-epitope specifics (which precise IgG constant-region residues) were not resolved at the level of this individual IGHG1 chain by the returned papers.

**VERDICT: YES**
